_findings.summary: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED: The keyModConstants legacy format [mod_idx1, mod_idx3] only captures keyMods at indices 1 and 3. When keyMods are at indices 0 and/or 2 (which happens in Templates B, C, and 98-opcode variants), they are silently lost. Three separate code paths propagate this data loss.

rootCause.title: keyModConstants legacy format loses keyMods at indices 0 and 2
rootCause.detail: The legacy keyModConstants format is a 2-element array: [keyMods[1], keyMods[3]]. This was originally correct for Template A where mods are at indices [1,3]. But other templates have mods at different index pairs: [0,2], [0,3], [1,2], [2,3]. When only keyModConstants is available and gets normalized back to keyMods[4], the conversion always maps to [0, kmc[0], 0, kmc[1]] = indices [1,3], losing data at [0] and [2].

bugLocations.issue: Only stores indices 1 and 3. If keyMods are at [0] or [2], they are discarded.
store() converts legacy format back, assuming indices [1,3]. Wrong for [0,2], [0,3], etc.
seed() same problem - when pipeline-config.json lacks keyMods, derives from keyModConstants with wrong index assumption.
_normalizeEntry() same problem - lookup() calls this to normalize old cache entries.
savePipelineConfig stores keyModConstants (lossy) but keyMods may also be present. Older configs had no keyMods field at all.

Template A (tdc.js).lost: NONE (indices [1,3] happen to be the correct ones)

secondaryFinding.title: Live CDN format change breaks the parser entirely
secondaryFinding.detail: ssl.captcha.qq.com now serves tdc.js in a packed/minified bootstrapper format (!function(){...}) instead of the raw VM code. vm-parser.js cannot find the dispatch switch in this format. This is a separate blocker from the keyMods issue.

analyzeTraceVerdict.title: analyzeTrace() Phase 4 works correctly
analyzeTraceVerdict.detail: The core trace analysis logic (Phase 4 keyMod detection) produces correct results for all tested source files. The k<=0 and k>=10M filters are safe. The cipher window size is adequate. The signed/unsigned comparison is correct. The problem is entirely in the keyModConstants serialization format and its lossy round-trip conversion.
analyzeTraceVerdict.evidence: All 6 saved targets produce correct keyMods when analyzed fresh via Puppeteer trace.

recommendedFixes: 1. In key-extractor.js: Remove the keyModConstants legacy format entirely, or fix it to store all 4 indices
2. In template-cache.js: Remove the _normalizeEntry conversion. Always require keyMods[4] in the cache.
3. In pipeline/run.js savePipelineConfig: Ensure keyMods is always saved to pipeline-config.json
4. Re-run the pipeline on all targets to regenerate pipeline-config.json with correct keyMods[4]
5. Regenerate the template cache from the corrected pipeline-config files
